title: Soil treatment for termites: Mchwatox 350 SC explained
description: Termites reach buildings through the soil. See how Mchwatox 350 SC imidacloprid termiticide is used before and after construction in Kenya.
answer: Mchwatox 350 SC is a suspension concentrate termiticide containing imidacloprid at 350 grams per litre, sold in a 1 litre bottle. It is used for soil treatment against termites, before a building goes up or around one that already stands. Dilute it as the label directs and wear protective gear.
intro: Termites work out of sight. They tunnel through the soil, reach a building at the foundation and can weaken doors, frames and roof timbers before anyone sees a sign. Treating the soil is one way to put a barrier between the colony and the structure.

sections.heading: What is Mchwatox 350 SC used for?
paragraphs: It is a termiticide for soil treatment in buildings and construction. It is used in two situations:
bullets: Pre-construction: before the slab or foundation is laid
Post-construction: on a building that already stands, around foundations, trenches and the perimeter, as the label directs

sections.heading: How is it applied?
paragraphs: Mchwatox 350 SC is a suspension concentrate (SC), so it is diluted with water exactly as the label directs. Apply the diluted liquid thoroughly and evenly to the soil, using the dilution and the volume of spray liquid printed on the label.
Start with an inspection to find where termites enter and where they nest. That tells you where the treatment matters most.

sections.heading: What should I do before treating the soil?
paragraphs: Give termites fewer reasons to stay near the building:
bullets: Fix leaking pipes and damp areas that keep the soil wet
Remove old tree stumps and buried timber near the building
Keep timber and firewood out of direct contact with the soil

sections.heading: What safety steps matter most?
paragraphs: Check the PCPB registration number on the label, and mix and apply exactly as directed. Wear gloves, a mask, overalls and boots, and avoid contact with skin and eyes. Keep the product away from children, pets, food, water sources and fish ponds.

Do not contaminate wells, boreholes or drains when you mix, spray or wash equipment. For a large building, a licensed pest control operator is a sensible choice. Keep the bottle closed, in a cool, dry, locked place.

faq: What is the active ingredient in Mchwatox 350 SC?
Imidacloprid at 350 grams per litre, formulated as a suspension concentrate. The exact strength and registration details are printed on the label.
Can I use it on a building that is already finished?
Yes. It is used for post-construction treatment of existing buildings, applied around the foundations, trenches and perimeter as the label describes.
Should I hire a professional to apply it?
For a large building, a licensed pest control operator is a sensible choice. Whoever applies it must follow the label for dilution, spray volume and safety.
closing: See the [[/p/mchwatox-350-sc-termiticide-1-litre.html|Mchwatox 350 SC product page]], browse [[/c/termite-control.html|termite control]], or read our [[/blog/termite-control-at-home-kenya.html|termite control guide]].

title: Metro 200SC termiticide for fence posts and small jobs
description: A 25 ml pack suits fence posts, timber and small soil treatments. See what Metro 200SC imidacloprid termiticide is used for in Kenya.
answer: Metro 200SC is a non-repellent, odourless and colourless suspension concentrate termiticide with imidacloprid at 200 grams per litre. It comes in a 25 ml pack for soil treatment, timber, posts and wooden fences. Dilute it as the label directs and mix only what the job needs.
intro: Subterranean termites live in the soil and travel through tunnels to reach fence posts, roof members and other wooden structures. A small, easy-to-store pack is often all a homeowner needs for a post, a fence line or a small treatment.

sections.heading: Why does a non-repellent termiticide matter?
paragraphs: A soil treatment places a protective zone between the termites and the structure you want to protect. Because Metro 200SC is non-repellent, termites do not easily detect and avoid the treated area.
It is also odourless and colourless, so nothing smells strongly in your home or compound.

sections.heading: What is the 25 ml pack good for?
paragraphs: The pack suits homeowners and small construction jobs. Typical uses include:
bullets: Soil treatment around small structures
The base of fence posts and timber before they go into the ground
Wooden fences and posts

sections.heading: How do I treat posts and soil?
paragraphs: Find the termite activity first: look for mud tubes on walls, hollow-sounding timber and soil mounds nearby. Then treat the soil thoroughly as directed on the label, and treat the base of fence posts and timber before they are placed in the ground.
The label gives the dilution. A 25 ml pack is small, so measure carefully and mix only what the job needs.

sections.heading: What should I do first, and how do I stay safe?
paragraphs: Remove rotting wood and tree stumps close to your building, repair leaks that keep the ground damp, and keep firewood and stored timber off the ground.

Check the PCPB registration number on the label, and mix and apply exactly as directed. Wear protective gear, keep Metro 200SC away from children, pets, food and water, and never contaminate water sources when you mix or spray.

faq: Will it leave a smell or a stain?
Metro 200SC is described as odourless and colourless, so it leaves no strong smell in your home or compound.
Can I treat a whole building with the 25 ml pack?
The pack suits homeowners, small construction jobs, posts and fences. For a whole building or a large infestation, consider a licensed pest control operator.
How should I store the pack?
Keep it tightly closed in its original container, in a cool, dry place out of reach of children and away from food.
closing: See the [[/p/metro-200sc-termiticide-25-ml.html|Metro 200SC product page]], browse [[/c/termite-control.html|termite control]], or read our [[/blog/termite-control-at-home-kenya.html|termite control guide]].

title: Premise 200 SC: choosing the 50 ml or 1 litre pack
description: Premise 200 SC lets termites carry the termiticide back to the colony. Compare the 50 ml and 1 litre packs for homes and building sites in Kenya.
answer: Bayer Premise 200 SC is a non-repellent, odourless termiticide with imidacloprid at 200 grams per litre. Termites cross the treated soil without detecting it and spread the active ingredient through the colony. The 50 ml pack suits a small job, and the 1 litre bottle suits a house or a building site.
intro: Termites (mchwa) rarely announce themselves. They eat door frames, roof timbers and cupboards from the inside until the damage is expensive. Premise 200 SC is made for soil treatment, and it comes in two pack sizes.

sections.heading: How does Premise 200 SC reach the whole colony?
paragraphs: It is non-repellent, so termites walk through the treated soil without detecting it. They carry the active ingredient back and spread it through the colony, which is how it reaches termites you cannot see.
It is suitable for pre-construction and post-construction treatment, and it is also listed for controlling ants.

sections.heading: Which pack should I choose?
paragraphs: The label rates make the choice simple. The 50 ml pack makes one 20 litre knapsack, which treats about 4 square metres of soil or 4 linear metres of trench. That suits a small job.
The 1 litre bottle makes twenty knapsacks, which suits a house or a building site. Check the rates against the label on your pack before mixing.

sections.heading: Where can it be applied?
paragraphs: The catalog lists these applications:
bullets: Foundations and slab preparation, before the slab is cast
Trenches along the inside and outside of foundation lines
Termite mounds and wall voids
Existing buildings, along foundations and slab joints

sections.heading: What safety steps matter most?
paragraphs: The product is harmful. Wear gloves, overalls, boots and a mask when mixing and spraying. It is toxic to bees and aquatic life, so never let spray or wash water reach streams, ponds, wells or drains.
Do not apply in rain or when rain is expected, and wash all equipment after use. For a large building, consider a licensed pest control operator.

faq: Is Premise 200 SC repellent to termites?
No. It is non-repellent, so termites cross the treated soil without detecting it and carry the active ingredient back to the colony.
Does it have a strong smell?
It is described as odourless, and practically odourless at the recommended dilution.
How should I store leftover product?
Store the unused product in its original, closed pack in a cool, dry, locked place, away from food, feed and children.
closing: See the [[/p/premise-200-sc-termiticide-50-ml.html|Premise 200 SC product page]] for both sizes, browse [[/c/termite-control.html|termite control]], or read our [[/blog/how-to-read-an-insecticide-label-kenya.html|guide to reading an insecticide label]].

title: Actellic 25EC: preparing a store before harvest
description: Spray empty stores and warehouses before stock goes in. Learn how Actellic 25EC pirimiphos-methyl insecticide is used for premises in Kenya.
answer: Actellic 25EC is an emulsifiable concentrate insecticide containing pirimiphos-methyl, sold in a 1 litre bottle for pest control in stores and premises. It is diluted with water as the label directs and sprayed on the surfaces of empty stores and warehouses before stock goes in.
intro: Insects in a store do their damage quietly, and by the time you notice them, stored produce can already be spoiled. Treating the building before the harvest arrives is one of the simplest ways to protect it.

sections.heading: What is Actellic 25EC used for?
paragraphs: It is used for pest control in stores and premises, such as empty grain stores and warehouses before stock goes in. It suits farmers preparing a store before harvest, traders and aggregators who hold produce, estate managers and institutions that keep food and feed.
Pest control operators who want a larger refill pack can also use the 1 litre bottle.

sections.heading: How do I prepare the store?
paragraphs: Cleaning comes before spraying. Residues and gaps give insects somewhere to survive between seasons:
bullets: Sweep out old grain and dust
Repair cracks and holes where insects hide
Remove spilled produce before spraying
Clean sacks, pallets and containers, because old residues carry pests from one season to the next
Use a sprayer that is kept for pesticides only

sections.heading: How is it applied?
paragraphs: As an emulsifiable concentrate, it is diluted with water as directed on the label and applied as a spray. Follow the label for the correct dilution, the surfaces to treat and any waiting period before food, feed or people return to the area.
Allow surfaces to dry as the label directs before storing grain or other produce. Stack new stock off the floor and away from the walls so that air can move and you can inspect it easily.

sections.heading: Is Actellic 25EC the same as Actellic 50EC?
paragraphs: No. They are separate products with their own labels and dilution rates, so never use the rate for one on the other.
Wear gloves, a mask, goggles and protective clothing when mixing and spraying, and keep the product away from children, pets, food and water. Never reuse the empty bottle.

faq: How do I mix it?
Dilute it with water exactly as the label directs. Do not guess the rate.
Where should I keep the bottle?
Keep it in the original, tightly closed bottle in a cool, dry, locked place, away from food, feed and direct sunlight.
Can I spray it near streams or ponds?
No. Do not contaminate food, feed, streams or ponds when you mix or spray.
closing: See the [[/p/actellic-25ec-insecticide-1-litre.html|Actellic 25EC product page]], browse [[/c/fumigation-chemicals.html|fumigation chemicals]], or read our [[/blog/how-to-read-an-insecticide-label-kenya.html|guide to reading an insecticide label]].

title: Actellic 50EC for stores, bagged grain and livestock houses
description: One pirimiphos-methyl concentrate, three jobs: store surfaces, bagged grain and grain admixture. See how Actellic 50EC is used in Kenya.
answer: Actellic 50EC is an organophosphate emulsifiable concentrate with pirimiphos-methyl at 500 grams per litre. It covers three jobs: surface spraying of stores and livestock houses, treating bagged grain, and mixing into stored grain as an admixture. Do not use it with thermal foggers.
intro: Weevils and moths can turn a full store of maize into dust within months. Insects arrive with the harvest and hide in cracks, on walls and on bag surfaces, so the building needs treating as well as the grain.

sections.heading: What can Actellic 50EC do?
paragraphs: It acts by contact, ingestion and fumigant action, and it keeps working on walls, floors and bag surfaces after you spray. The catalog lists weevils, beetles, moths, flies and wasps. It is sold in four sizes: 100 ml, 250 ml, 500 ml and 1 litre.
Its three uses are:
bullets: Surface spray for walls, floors, empty stores and livestock houses
Treatment of bagged grain and bag stacks
Admixture mixed into stored grain

sections.heading: How do I use it?
paragraphs: Clean and sweep the store first, removing old grain and debris, then spray to wet all surfaces without run-off. For admixture, dilute the measured amount in the water volume shown on the label and apply it to the grain, not in the knapsack.
The catalog publishes mixing rates and coverage for each use, so check them against the label on your pack before you mix. Measure the area first, so that you mix only the volume you need.

sections.heading: Can I use it in a thermal fogger?
paragraphs: No. The catalog advice for this product is not to use it with thermal foggers. If you own a fogging machine, choose a product whose label allows thermal fogging.

sections.heading: What safety steps matter most?
paragraphs: Actellic 50EC is an organophosphate, so wear gloves, a mask and overalls when mixing and spraying, and keep children, pets, food, feed and water away. Remove food, feed and animals before spraying, and ventilate the store afterwards.
Label grain treated by admixture as chemically treated, and follow any waiting period on the pack. Store the bottle closed, in its original container, in a cool, dry, locked place.

faq: Which pests does Actellic 50EC control?
The catalog lists weevils, beetles, moths, flies and wasps.
Does it keep working after I spray?
Yes. It keeps working on treated walls, floors and bag surfaces after you spray.
Do porous surfaces need more spray liquid?
They can. Surfaces such as concrete, brick and unpainted wood may need more spray liquid than normal surfaces, so check the label.
closing: See the [[/p/actellic-50ec-insecticide-1-litre.html|Actellic 50EC product page]] for every size, browse [[/c/fumigation-chemicals.html|fumigation chemicals]], or read our [[/blog/how-to-read-an-insecticide-label-kenya.html|guide to reading an insecticide label]].

title: Actellic Gold Dust: protecting stored maize at home
description: A ready-to-use dust you mix through grain as it goes into storage. See what Actellic Gold Dust protects against and how to use it in Kenya.
answer: Actellic Gold Dust is a ready-to-use dustable powder for protecting stored grain from insect damage. It combines two active ingredients, pirimiphos-methyl and thiamethoxam, and needs no mixing in water. You mix it evenly through the grain as it goes into storage.
intro: Stored-grain pests can ruin a harvest in a few months, hollowing out kernels, leaving dust and spoiling grain for food, seed and sale. A dust that goes in as the grain is stored keeps working inside the bag.

sections.heading: What does Actellic Gold Dust protect against?
paragraphs: The catalog lists the larger grain borer, grain weevil, red flour beetle, lesser grain borer and other stored-grain beetles and moths.
It is registered in Kenya by the Pest Control Products Board, and the registration number is printed on the pack. Check it there.

sections.heading: How do I use it?
paragraphs: Mix the dust evenly through the grain as it goes into storage. Even mixing matters, because pests survive in untreated pockets, so turn the grain until the dust is spread through every bag.

The pack prints a rate for a standard bag of grain. At that rate, a 100 g pack treats about two bags, a 500 g pack about ten and a 1 kg pack about twenty. Follow the label exactly and do not use more than directed.

sections.heading: How should I prepare the store and the grain?
paragraphs: Treatment works well in a clean, dry store:
bullets: Clean and dry the store, and use dry, clean bags
Remove old grain, sweep out dust and fix cracks where insects can hide
Make sure the grain is properly dry before storing, because damp grain spoils even when treated

sections.heading: Which pack size should I pick?
paragraphs: There are three sizes: 100 g, 500 g and 1 kg. They suit households and small farms storing maize and other cereals.
Avoid breathing the dust, and wear a mask and gloves when mixing. Keep it away from children, pets and food, and follow the label's waiting period before using treated grain.

faq: Do I mix it with water?
No. It is a ready-to-use dust that is mixed evenly through the grain as it goes into storage.
How should I store the pack?
Keep the pack closed in a cool, dry place out of reach of children.
Can I rinse containers into a stream or pond?
No. Do not rinse containers into water sources.
closing: See the [[/p/actellic-gold-dust-1-kg.html|Actellic Gold Dust product page]] for all sizes, browse [[/c/fumigation-chemicals.html|fumigation chemicals]], or read our [[/blog/how-to-buy-agrovet-products-online-kenya.html|guide to buying agrovet products online]].

title: Grain-Save Dust: permethrin for stored maize and beans
description: Protect stored maize and beans from weevils. See how Grain-Save Dust permethrin protectant is used, and why you should not double-treat grain.
answer: Grain-Save Dust is a permethrin-based dust that protects stored maize and beans against weevils and other storage pests. It is mixed into dry grain at the rate printed on the label and comes in a 500 g pack suited to farmers and households storing grain.
intro: After harvest, weevils can hollow out kernels, leave dust and holes, lower germination and make grain unfit for food or sale. Losses can be heavy within a few months, especially in warm, humid stores.

sections.heading: What does Grain-Save Dust protect?
paragraphs: It protects stored maize and beans against weevils and other storage pests. Treating grain as it goes into storage protects the work you put into the crop and keeps seed and food grain in good condition for longer.

sections.heading: How do I mix it into grain?
paragraphs: Make sure the grain is properly dry before storage, because damp grain spoils even when treated. Mix the dust into the dry grain at the label rate, turning the grain thoroughly so the dust is spread evenly through every bag or heap.
Even mixing is important, because untreated pockets let pests survive. Put the treated grain into clean, dry bags or containers, and store it off the ground and away from walls.

sections.heading: Can I add it to grain that was already treated?
paragraphs: No. Using two protectants on the same grain can leave too much residue. If you are not sure whether your grain has been treated, do not add more.
Before you start, sweep out old grain and dust, repair cracks and holes, and keep the store dry and well ventilated. Check stored grain regularly for live insects, holes and powdery dust.

sections.heading: What safety steps matter most?
paragraphs: Read the label before use. Wear a mask, gloves and protective clothing when mixing, and avoid breathing the dust. Follow the label's waiting period before using treated grain.
Do not feed treated grain to animals unless the label allows it. Permethrin is very toxic to fish, so never rinse containers or equipment into streams, ponds or drains.

faq: What is Grain-Save Dust used for?
It protects stored maize and beans against weevils and other storage pests.
Can I feed treated grain to animals?
Not unless the label allows it. Read the label for the waiting period and for any limits on feed use.
Where should I keep the pack?
Keep the pack closed in a cool, dry, locked place away from food and feed.
closing: See the [[/p/grain-save-dust-permethrin-500-g.html|Grain-Save Dust product page]], browse [[/c/fumigation-chemicals.html|fumigation chemicals]], or read our [[/blog/how-to-read-an-insecticide-label-kenya.html|guide to reading an insecticide label]].

title: Thermal fogging machine: what it does and what goes in
description: A pulse thermal fogger spreads fog into corners and crevices. See what the machine is for, and what to check before choosing an insecticide.
answer: The Thermal Fogging Machine Pulsed Power Sprayer is a professional pulse thermal fogger for mosquito, fly and pest control and fumigation, with dual tanks and stainless steel heat pipes. It is equipment, not an insecticide, so pair it with a product whose label allows thermal fogging.
intro: Mosquitoes, flies and other pests hide in corners and crevices that a hand sprayer reaches slowly. A fog spreads through a space, which is why fogging is used where pests hide in cracks and corners.

sections.heading: What is the machine used for?
paragraphs: It is sold as a single unit for farms, greenhouses, warehouses and residential areas. Its features include:
bullets: A pulse thermal fogger for mosquito, fly and pest control and fumigation
Durable dual tanks
Stainless steel heat pipes
Fast, efficient fog distribution that reaches crevices and corners

sections.heading: Which insecticide goes in the tanks?
paragraphs: The catalog does not name one. Choose a product whose label allows thermal fogging, and follow that label for the dilution and the time the space must stay closed.
For example, the catalog advice for Actellic 50EC says it must not be used with thermal foggers. Read every insecticide label before you fill a tank.

sections.heading: How do I start and stop it?
paragraphs: The catalog does not list the fuel type, tank capacity, output or settings, so follow the manufacturer's manual for filling, start-up and shut-down.
Treat only the space you have prepared, and let the machine cool before you handle or move it.

sections.heading: How do I stay safe around a thermal fogger?
paragraphs: The machine gets hot, so never touch the heat pipes while it is running or cooling. Remove people, pets, food, feed and animals from the space, and keep flammable materials away from the machine and its hot parts.

Wear the protective equipment named on the insecticide label, including a respirator if the label requires one, and do not enter a fogged space until the label says it is safe. Keep the machine away from children.

faq: Does the machine come with insecticide?
No. It is the equipment only, sold as 1 unit. You choose a suitable insecticide separately.
Where can I use it?
The catalog lists farms, greenhouses, warehouses and residential areas.
How should I store it?
Let the machine cool completely, empty the tanks as the manual directs, and store it dry and out of reach of children, away from food and feed.
closing: See the [[/p/thermal-fogging-machine-pulsed-power-sprayer-1-unit.html|Thermal Fogging Machine product page]], browse [[/c/fumigation-chemicals.html|fumigation chemicals]], or read our [[/blog/how-to-read-an-insecticide-label-kenya.html|guide to reading an insecticide label]].
